pause.name: Pause
pause.description: Suppress the bridge's effect on its lights for a short duration, then resume automatically. For radio-airtime contention — nothing about what these lights should look like has changed, so the session (if any) is left alone and resumes normally once the pause ends.

seconds.name: Seconds
seconds.description: How long to pause for. 0 uses a healthy default (a couple of seconds).

resume.name: Resume
resume.description: Cancel an in-progress pause early. No effect if nothing is paused, or if a release is in progress.

release.name: Release
release.description: Stop driving these lights until a new session genuinely begins — for an intent change (e.g. a lighting sweep) rather than a brief courtesy gap. Discards the pending restore target immediately, so a session ending afterwards won't relight whatever the caller just set. Asks a compliant TV to stop via the stream-active flag; if it doesn't within the given grace period, forces the same clean teardown regardless.

seconds.name: Seconds
seconds.description: Grace period to wait for the TV to comply before forcing it. 0 uses a healthy default (a couple of seconds).

not_paired.description: Your TV did not pair within 60 seconds. The bridge will start without a paired TV — you can pair later from the integration's Configure menu.

init.title: Hue Entertainment Bridge

data_description.pair_now: Opens a 60-second pairing window after saving.
data_description.bind_ip: Leave blank to use the auto-detected HA host IP. Set to a secondary IP address (e.g. a macvlan interface) to bind the bridge's HTTP and DTLS servers to that address only, freeing port 80 on the primary IP for Traefik or Nginx.
data_description.http_mode: Where the Hue REST API is served. Automatic: uses Home Assistant's own web server when it listens on port 80 without HTTPS (Settings → System → Network, HA 2026.8+), otherwise a standalone server on port 80. Change only if the automatic choice is wrong.
